# Vendored official ECCO tutorial helpers

## `ecco_po_tutorials.py`

This is the **official** ECCO v4 Python Tutorial helper module, vendored verbatim so our
skills can use it as a **Rung-1 verification reference** (see `docs/verify.md`) — i.e. we
check our own calculations against the tutorial authors' own code.

- **Source:** https://github.com/ECCO-GROUP/ECCO-v4-Python-Tutorial
- **Path in repo:** `Intro_to_PO_Tutorials/ecco_po_tutorials.py`
- **Branch:** `master`
- **Commit:** `3f0fcca17c79f622b03bf9c49ff37843191d5afe`
- **Vendored:** 2026-07-25
- **Not on PyPI / not pip-installable** — the tutorials have users download it manually,
  which is why we vendor a pinned copy rather than depend on an install.

Key functions used for verification:
- `geos_vel_compute(dens_press_filename, grid_filename, subset=None)` — reference
  geostrophic-velocity calculation (returns `u_g`, `v_g` in **model x/y** coordinates).
- `mean_weighted_binned`, `llc_grid_idx_along_lat`, `data_along_lat`,
  `depth_two_subplots`, `plot_mask` — transect/plotting helpers used by the PO tutorials.

**Do not edit this file.** It is a pinned upstream reference; our code is verified
*against* it, not the other way around. To update, re-fetch from the pinned repo and bump
the commit hash above.

## `jmd95.py`

The canonical MITgcm **Jackett & McDougall (1995)** equation of state (seawater density
from salinity, potential temperature, pressure). The Steric Height tutorial imports it
(`from jmd95 import densjmd95`), and it is **not in `ecco_v4_py`, the vendored
`ecco_po_tutorials.py`, or as a PyPI package** in our pinned env (gsw/TEOS-10 is also not
installed) — so we vendor it. Used by `compute-steric-height` for the reference specific-
volume profile and the thermosteric/halosteric decomposition.

- **Source:** https://github.com/ECCO-GROUP/ECCO-v4-Python-Tutorial
- **Path in repo:** `misc/jmd95.py` (the `Intro_to_PO_Tutorials/jmd95.py` path is a pointer)
- **Commit:** `3f0fcca17c79f622b03bf9c49ff37843191d5afe` (same pin as above)
- **Vendored:** 2026-08-05
- **Only modification:** `np.asfarray(x)` → `np.asarray(x, dtype=float)` (6 sites) —
  `np.asfarray` was removed in NumPy 2.0 (our env pins `numpy>=2.5`); the two are exactly
  equivalent. **No numerical change:** the published check value
  `densjmd95(35.5, 3, 3000) = 1041.83267 kg/m³` still reproduces to <1e-3 (asserted in
  `compute-steric-height/scripts/test_steric.py`).

Provides `densjmd95(s, theta, p)` (p in **dbar**) and `bulkmodjmd95`. This is a Rung-1
anchor for the steric skill's EOS: it carries its own published check value.
